## Overview

**Core question:** Can the H.264 and H.265 encode paths produce decodable video with the requested picture, resource, rate-control, query, and intra-refresh behavior?

- This page covers the implementation and registration in [`vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3979-L4015), which creates the `video.encode.h264` and `video.encode.h265` test families.
- Each registered leaf is instantiated for layered or separated source images and for video or general image layouts. The leaf name selects the encode behavior, while the codec selects the H.264 or H.265 structures and capability fields.
- The test uploads YUV 4:2:0 frames, creates a video encode session and DPB, records `vkCmdEncodeVideoKHR` calls, collects encoded bytes, decodes the resulting H.264 or H.265 byte stream, and compares decoded frames with the input.
- The page explains the registered leaves, clip dimensions, GOP and reference patterns, resource layouts, feature gates, capability-based pruning, host-side execution, and the checks that turn an encoded stream into a CTS result.

## Background Knowledge

- A video encode operation reads an encode input picture and optional active reference pictures, writes compressed data to a bitstream buffer, and can place a reconstructed picture in a DPB slot. This operation model is needed to understand how reference pictures and reconstructed pictures participate in encoding. See the [video encode operation model](../../../../vulkan-docs/src/chapters/video/encode.adoc#L8-L11) and [operation steps](../../../../vulkan-docs/src/chapters/video/encode.adoc#L199-L235).
- H.264 pictures use macroblocks and H.264 slices. H.265 pictures use coding tree units, coding units, slices, slice segments, and tiles. The distinction matters for codec-specific picture information and for calculating intra-refresh regions. See [H.264 picture types and coding blocks](../../../../vulkan-docs/src/chapters/video/h264_encode.adoc#L207-L265) and [H.265 picture types and coding blocks](../../../../vulkan-docs/src/chapters/video/h265_encode.adoc#L240-L301).

## Registration Hierarchy

```text
video.encode
├── h264
└── h265
```

The leaves under both codec families are generated by the same test-definition table. The concrete executable names append `_layered_src_general_layout`, `_layered_src_video_layout`, `_separated_src_general_layout`, or `_separated_src_video_layout` to the selected leaf name.

## Behavior Parameters

The primary behavioral axis is the registered encode behavior leaf. The codec is a parallel axis because it changes the codec-specific syntax and capabilities while preserving the host-side test shape.

### `i` , one IDR picture

The test encodes one IDR picture without active references. It checks the basic profile, session, source-image, bitstream, and decode path for the selected codec. The definition uses one GOP with an `{IDR_FRAME}` pattern ([`g_EncodeTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L432-L445), [`g_EncodeTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L751-L763)).

### `rc_vbr` , variable bitrate control

The test enables `VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_VBR_BIT_KHR` and uses the same basic frame shape. It exercises the rate-control state that is applied before the later encode operations in a GOP ([`setupRateControl`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2863-L2930)).

### `rc_cbr` , constant bitrate control

The test enables `VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_CBR_BIT_KHR`. Its failure is about the CBR setup or the resulting encoded quality, not about an exact encoded byte sequence.

### `rc_disable` , disabled rate control

The test selects `VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_DISABLED_BIT_KHR` and supplies constant QP 28 to the encoded slices. It uses an IDR followed by a P picture and applies the lower ordinary PSNR threshold used for this mode ([`initializeTestParameters`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2027-L2034), [`setupRateControl`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2878-L2929)).

### `quality_level` , quality level zero

The test selects encode quality level zero and sends the corresponding quality control to the coding scope. The source checks that the selected level is less than the queried `maxQualityLevels` ([`initializeTestParameters`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2057-L2058), [`encodeFrame`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3127-L3143)).

### `quantization_map_delta_rc_vbr`, `quantization_map_delta_rc_cbr`, and `quantization_map_delta_rc_disable` , delta maps with rate control variants

These leaves combine a delta quantization map with VBR, CBR, or disabled rate control. The test obtains the map format and texel size from video format properties, creates map images, and adds `VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_WITH_QUANTIZATION_DELTA_MAP_BIT_KHR` to the encode flags ([`setupQuantizationMapResources`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2278-L2482), [`getEncodeFlags`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3767-L3780)).

### `quantization_map_delta` , delta-map effect

The test prepares three one-frame GOP iterations. The first two maps use constant values, while the third map gives the left and right halves different delta values. The source contains a frame-2 left-versus-right PSNR comparison, but its low-PSNR handling can exit the verification loop at frame 1 before that comparison is reached.

### `quantization_map_emphasis_cbr` and `quantization_map_emphasis_vbr` , emphasis maps with rate control variants

These leaves combine an emphasis map with CBR or VBR. The second map uses zero emphasis on one side and maximum emphasis on the other when the selected map format permits it. The test checks that the second frame's PSNR difference is greater than the first frame's difference.

### `usage` , non-default encode usage

The test selects streaming usage, desktop content, and high-quality tuning instead of the default usage, content, and tuning values when it creates the encode profile ([`initializeTestParameters`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2039-L2048)).

### `i_p` , IDR followed by P

The test encodes an IDR followed by a P picture in encode and submission order. The P picture refers to the preceding reconstructed picture through the configured DPB slot ([`g_EncodeTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L589-L601), [`encodeFrame`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3044-L3112)).

### `i_p_not_matching_order` , recording order differs from submission order

The test records the same IDR and P behavior with the P command buffer recorded first, then submits the IDR command buffer before the P command buffer. It uses a semaphore between submissions and reserves safe bitstream offsets while recording the P command ([`g_EncodeTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L602-L614), [`handleSwapOrderSubmission`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3334-L3356)).

### `i_p_b_13` , two GOPs with P and B pictures

The test encodes two 14-picture GOPs. Each pattern contains an IDR, P, and B pictures, with frame indices reordered so that display or frame numbering differs from command order. H.264 uses up to four reference frames in the definition; H.265 uses two. The per-picture L0 and L1 reference lists and DPB slots are explicit in [`g_EncodeTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L667-L703) and [`g_EncodeTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L985-L1021).

### `query_with_status` , completion status in encode feedback

The test uses encode feedback queries and requires the selected query result status to be `VK_QUERY_RESULT_STATUS_COMPLETE_KHR`. Query support is checked from queue-family properties before execution ([`checkQueryResultSupport`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L1951-L1976), [`processQueryPoolResults`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L1412-L1433)).

### `inline_query` , inline encode query

The test creates the session with `VK_VIDEO_SESSION_CREATE_INLINE_QUERIES_BIT_KHR` and attaches `VkVideoInlineQueryInfoKHR` to the codec-specific picture information instead of using `vkCmdBeginQuery` and `vkCmdEndQuery` ([`createVideoSession`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2240-L2276), [`encodeFrame`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3279-L3319)).

### `resources_without_profiles` , profile-independent resources

The test creates source images without a `VkVideoProfileListInfoKHR` and sets `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_VIDEO_PROFILE_INDEPENDENT_BIT_KHR`. The encode profile remains attached to the session and encode buffer, so this leaf tests resource compatibility rather than removing profile requirements from the operation ([`prepareInputImages`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2691-L2728)).

### `resolution_change_dpb` , half-resolution second GOP

The test uses two session-parameter objects. The second has half the original width and height, and frames after the first GOP use the smaller coded extent. The source also checks each extent against the queried minimum and maximum coded extents ([`setupSessionParameters`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2506-L2569), [`currentCodedExtent`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2665-L2688)).

### `intra_refresh_picture_partition`, `intra_refresh_any_block_based`, `intra_refresh_row_based`, and `intra_refresh_column_based` , regular intra refresh modes

These leaves enable per-picture partition, block-based, block-row-based, or block-column-based intra refresh. The test derives the supported region count from codec coding-block geometry, the intra-refresh capability, and the slice or slice-segment limit. It then adds `VkVideoEncodeIntraRefreshInfoKHR` to eligible frames and updates reference-slot refresh state ([`queryIntraRefreshCapabilities`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3535-L3708), [`createIntraRefreshInfo`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3710-L3730)).

### `intra_refresh_any_block_based_empty_region`, `intra_refresh_row_based_empty_region`, and `intra_refresh_column_based_empty_region` , empty refresh region

These leaves use the selected block geometry but set the intra-refresh cycle duration to the capability's maximum and apply the refresh to only one frame. This checks the empty-region form rather than a normal complete refresh cycle.

### `intra_refresh_picture_partition_midway`, `intra_refresh_any_block_based_midway`, `intra_refresh_row_based_midway`, and `intra_refresh_column_based_midway` , refresh cycle restart

These leaves use a seven-frame pattern. Frames 1 and 2 continue the first cycle, frame 3 starts a new cycle, and frames 4 through 6 continue it with indices 1, 2, and 3. The source requires a cycle duration of at least 4 for these cases ([`queryIntraRefreshCapabilities`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3690-L3700), [`getIntraRefreshIndex`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3783-L3803)).

## Shader Analysis

This test has no shader. Its device-side work uses Vulkan video commands and H.264 or H.265 Video Std structures, so a shader walkthrough would not describe the tested behavior. The source-reviewed exception entry for `Encode.md` records this page's no-walkthrough status.

## Runtime Execution and Result Checking

- `iterate` initializes the selected codec and leaf, chooses the source clip dimensions, selects formats and queues, validates capabilities, creates the encode session, prepares optional quantization maps and session parameters, creates DPB and source resources, allocates the bitstream buffer and queries, uploads frames, configures rate control, records commands, submits them, and verifies the encoded stream ([`iterate`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3819-L3838)).
- The test accepts `VK_FORMAT_G8_B8R8_2PLANE_420_UNORM` for both the encode source and DPB after querying supported video formats ([`setupDeviceAndQueues`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2082-L2111)).
- The source clip is loaded as I420 input. `loadVideoFrames` extracts each frame, converts it to I420 for host-side comparison, uploads the source image, and limits processing to the number of complete frames available in the clip ([`loadVideoFrames`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2730-L2797)).
- The test prefixes the encoded session headers to the host-visible encode buffer. Each `vkCmdEncodeVideoKHR` writes one frame's bitstream range. Query feedback reports bytes written and the next offset is aligned to `minBitstreamBufferOffsetAlignment` ([`encodeFrames`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2941-L2979), [`processQueryPoolResults`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L1412-L1433)).
- The encoder records codec-specific picture information. P pictures use L0 references; B pictures use L0 and L1 references. Every encoded picture has a setup reference slot, and the DPB resource is selected according to the test definition ([`encodeFrame`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3044-L3112), [`prepareDPBResources`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2572-L2663)).
- The validator constructs an H.264 or H.265 byte-stream demuxer and a basic decoder, decodes the expected processed frames, converts decoded NV12 output to I420, and computes PSNR against the corresponding input vector ([`verifyEncodedBitstream`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3394-L3447)).
- Ordinary cases require PSNR of at least 30.0. Disabled-rate-control cases use 20.0. A value above 10.0 but below the applicable lower threshold returns a quality warning; a value at or below 10.0 fails. The test does not require encoded byte equality.
- Quantization-map checks add a feature-specific condition. For emphasis maps, frame 1 must have a larger PSNR difference than frame 0. For delta maps, frame 2 must not produce a positive left-versus-right PSNR difference. If a mapped frame at index 1 is below the ordinary PSNR threshold, the source breaks out of the verification loop and returns the pass result instead of applying that threshold or reaching later frame checks ([`verifyEncodedBitstream`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3448-L3504)).
- If the decoder yields fewer frames than expected, the test raises an internal error. Otherwise it returns a pass with the number of correctly encoded frames.

## Failure Meaning

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `i` | Basic codec profile, session, I-picture setup, source-image access, or bitstream production. |
| `rc_vbr` | VBR capability, rate-control state, or encoded quality. |
| `rc_cbr` | CBR capability, rate-control state, or encoded quality. |
| `rc_disable` | Disabled-rate-control constant-QP path or encoded quality. |
| `quality_level` | Quality-level state or its effect on encoded quality. |
| `quantization_map_delta_rc_vbr` | Delta-map resource/session setup combined with VBR encoding. |
| `quantization_map_delta_rc_cbr` | Delta-map resource/session setup combined with CBR encoding. |
| `quantization_map_delta_rc_disable` | Delta-map resource/session setup combined with constant-QP encoding. |
| `quantization_map_delta` | Delta-map resource/session setup or delta-map effect on PSNR distribution. |
| `quantization_map_emphasis_cbr` | Emphasis-map resource/session setup combined with CBR encoding. |
| `quantization_map_emphasis_vbr` | Emphasis-map resource/session setup combined with VBR encoding. |
| `usage` | Non-default encode usage state or its effect on encoded quality. |
| `i_p` | P-picture reference-slot setup, forward prediction, or frame ordering. |
| `i_p_not_matching_order` | Command submission order, synchronization, or deferred bitstream-offset handling. |
| `i_p_b_13` | H.264/H.265 P/B reference lists, DPB slot lifetime, frame numbering, or reordered pictures. |
| `resolution_change_dpb` | Second session-parameter set, half-resolution picture resources, or resolution transition handling. |
| `query_with_status` | Encode feedback query status, query-result support, or completion handling. |
| `inline_query` | Inline-query session creation, query association, or inline feedback handling. |
| `resources_without_profiles` | Video-profile-independent source/DPB resource compatibility. |
| `intra_refresh_picture_partition` | Per-picture-partition intra-refresh indices, slice count, or DPB updates. |
| `intra_refresh_any_block_based` | Block-based intra-refresh mode or refreshed-region handling. |
| `intra_refresh_row_based` | Block-row intra-refresh mode or row-region handling. |
| `intra_refresh_column_based` | Block-column intra-refresh mode or column-region handling. |
| `intra_refresh_any_block_based_empty_region` | Empty-region block-based intra-refresh control or cycle-duration handling. |
| `intra_refresh_row_based_empty_region` | Empty-region row-based intra-refresh control or cycle-duration handling. |
| `intra_refresh_column_based_empty_region` | Empty-region column-based intra-refresh control or cycle-duration handling. |
| `intra_refresh_picture_partition_midway` | Starting a new per-picture-partition refresh cycle mid-way through the sequence. |
| `intra_refresh_any_block_based_midway` | Starting a new block-based refresh cycle mid-way through the sequence. |
| `intra_refresh_row_based_midway` | Starting a new row-based refresh cycle mid-way through the sequence. |
| `intra_refresh_column_based_midway` | Starting a new column-based refresh cycle mid-way through the sequence. |

The same leaf names are registered under both codecs. The codec selects the H.264 or H.265 profile-specific parameter structures, picture syntax, and capability fields; it does not change the host-side PSNR contract.

### Cause Analysis

#### Codec session or basic picture setup

**Possible failure symptoms:** The test may reject the required format or capability, fail while creating or submitting the session, produce fewer decoded frames, or return a PSNR failure for `i`.

**Possible implementation causes:** The source checks the selected encode profile, session parameters, source and DPB image compatibility, and the codec-specific structures required by the H.264 or H.265 encode operation. A failure in this path needs source-level and validation-layer investigation to distinguish unsupported functionality from an implementation error.

#### Rate control, quality level, or encode usage

**Possible failure symptoms:** `rc_vbr`, `rc_cbr`, `rc_disable`, `quality_level`, or `usage` can fail through an unsupported capability, an incomplete query result, a submission error, or a decoded frame below the mode's PSNR threshold.

**Possible implementation causes:** The implementation may expose a rate-control mode or quality level inconsistently with the state accepted by the encode command, or the resulting control state may produce output below the CTS quality threshold. The source does not require a particular bitrate or encoded byte pattern, so a PSNR failure needs codec and driver investigation rather than a byte-for-byte comparison.

#### Quantization-map setup or effect

**Possible failure symptoms:** Map cases can fail while querying a map format, creating or populating map images, attaching map state, or checking the frame-specific PSNR relationship. The emphasis case fails if frame 1 does not have the larger PSNR difference. The delta case fails if frame 2 has a positive left-versus-right difference.

**Possible implementation causes:** The cause may be an unsupported map capability, an incorrect map image layout or texel-size interpretation, a session-parameter compatibility problem, or an encoder that does not apply the supplied delta or emphasis values as requested. The exact map effect is intentionally evaluated through the source's PSNR relationship, not through a fixed bitstream.

#### Reference pictures, DPB, and ordering

**Possible failure symptoms:** `i_p` or `i_p_b_13` can fail during reference-slot setup, decode with missing or reordered frames, or PSNR comparison. `i_p_not_matching_order` can fail when the swapped submissions complete or when query feedback produces an incorrect bitstream offset.

**Possible implementation causes:** A driver or hardware implementation may mishandle active reference slots, reconstructed-picture setup, P/B reference-list interpretation, command synchronization, or bitstream writes that complete in a different submission order. The source defines the slot and list relationships explicitly, while the Vulkan specification defines active references and reconstructed-picture information in [`VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR`](../../../../vulkan-docs/src/chapters/video/encode.adoc#L795-L846).

#### Resolution and profile-independent resources

**Possible failure symptoms:** `resolution_change_dpb` can fail at extent validation, session-parameter selection, resource binding, decode, or PSNR. `resources_without_profiles` can fail while creating or using source images that omit the profile list.

**Possible implementation causes:** The implementation may reject a legal extent transition, associate the wrong parameter set with the second GOP, or mishandle the compatibility rules for `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_VIDEO_PROFILE_INDEPENDENT_BIT_KHR`. The source-level evidence identifies these operations, but a precise driver or hardware cause requires investigation of the failing API call and validation output.

#### Query completion and inline queries

**Possible failure symptoms:** `query_with_status` can report a status other than `VK_QUERY_RESULT_STATUS_COMPLETE_KHR`, while `inline_query` can fail at session creation, query association, query availability, or bytes-written processing.

**Possible implementation causes:** The queue family may not expose the required status-query support, or the implementation may mishandle query reset, inline query indexing, completion, or encode feedback. The source checks status only when the leaf requests it and otherwise still uses bytes-written feedback to advance the buffer.

#### Intra-refresh regions and cycle state

**Possible failure symptoms:** Intra-refresh leaves can be pruned before execution, fail when the requested slice or slice-segment count exceeds a capability, or produce decoded frames that do not meet the PSNR check. Midway cases can fail when the second cycle starts at the wrong index; empty-region cases can fail when the maximum cycle duration is not handled.

**Possible implementation causes:** Possible causes include incorrect support reporting for an intra-refresh mode, wrong coding-block-to-region calculation, incorrect `intraRefreshIndex` or cycle duration handling, failure to carry dirty refresh regions through the reference slot, or codec-specific slice and slice-segment construction errors. The source attaches refresh state only to eligible frames and updates reference-slot metadata for later frames ([`updateReferenceSlotsForIntraRefresh`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3732-L3765)).

## Case Pruning

### Requirement-based pruning

- Every case requires video encode support for the selected codec and `VK_KHR_synchronization2` ([`checkSupport`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3868-L3874)). H.264 leaves require `VK_KHR_video_encode_h264`; H.265 leaves require `VK_KHR_video_encode_h265`.
- `inline_query` and `resources_without_profiles` additionally require `VK_KHR_video_maintenance1`. Quantization-map leaves require `VK_KHR_video_encode_quantization_map`. Intra-refresh leaves require `VK_KHR_video_encode_intra_refresh` ([`checkSupport`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3887-L3956)).
- The implementation must expose the selected source and DPB format. It must also expose P-picture support for P leaves and B-picture support through the relevant L0 or L1 capability for B leaves ([`setupDeviceAndQueues`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2082-L2111), [`queryAndValidateCapabilities`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2189-L2211)).
- VBR and CBR leaves require the corresponding rate-control mode and a nonzero maximum bitrate. Delta and emphasis leaves require the matching encode capability flags. The requested DPB slot count must not exceed `maxDpbSlots`, and quality level zero must be below `maxQualityLevels` ([`queryAndValidateCapabilities`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2165-L2237)).
- `query_with_status` is skipped when no queue family reports query-result status support. The general-layout variants require `VK_KHR_unified_image_layouts` and the `unifiedImageLayoutsVideo` feature ([`checkQueryResultSupport`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L1951-L1976), [`checkSupport`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3962-L3969)).
- The selected coded extent must be within the queried `minCodedExtent` and `maxCodedExtent`. Resolution-change frames use half the original extent after the first GOP and are checked against those limits ([`currentCodedExtent`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2665-L2688)).
- Intra-refresh cases require the requested mode, region count, cycle duration, and slice or slice-segment count to fit the queried capabilities. Midway cases require a maximum cycle duration of at least 4 ([`queryIntraRefreshCapabilities`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3535-L3708)).

This pruning means the case is unsupported or not legal for the current implementation. It is not a failed encode result.

### Design-based pruning

- The test definition uses fixed clips, GOP patterns, reference lists, and option combinations. The four resource/layout suffixes are generated for every leaf instead of creating an independent parameter matrix in the definition ([`createVideoEncodeTests`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3986-L4007)).
- Quantization-map cases use two or three maps only where a second or third frame is needed to compare map effects. They do not combine every map type with every rate-control mode.
- Basic intra-refresh cases clamp the frame pattern to the supported cycle duration plus the initial IDR. Empty-region cases use one refreshed frame, and midway cases use a fixed seven-frame sequence with a cycle restart. These choices keep the registered cases tied to the intended refresh behavior rather than enumerating unsupported or redundant combinations ([`queryIntraRefreshCapabilities`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L3684-L3707)).
- If a clip contains fewer complete frames than requested, `loadVideoFrames` processes only the available frames. For intra refresh it also clamps the GOP frame count before resource preparation and encoding ([`loadVideoFrames`](../../../modules/vulkan/video/vktVideoEncodeTests.cpp#L2730-L2758)).

## Key Takeaways

- The behavior leaf selects the encode feature or picture pattern; H.264 and H.265 share the host-side flow but use different codec-specific structures and capability checks.
- Every leaf has four registered resource/layout forms, so failures can be isolated to layered versus separated source images and to video versus general image layouts.
- P and B cases are reference-management tests as well as encode tests. The source explicitly defines frame order, reference lists, DPB slots, and reconstructed-picture setup.
- The result check validates decodability, processed frame count, and PSNR. Quantization-map leaves add their own frame and half-frame PSNR relationships.
- A capability rejection is a requirement-based skip. A decoded-frame, query-status, or PSNR failure means the selected supported path did not meet the behavior checked by that leaf.
